study_type.note: Qualitative descriptive case study (Yin) based on interviews and an open questionnaire.

research_method.claude: Qualitative descriptive case study (Yin): 6 semi-structured interviews with professors and an open questionnaire to students; thematic analysis (Braun & Clarke), inductive then compared with SPACE
research_method.nlm: Descriptive case study: semi-structured interviews, questionnaires, thematic analysis; findings compared/categorized against SPACE
research_method.value: Qualitative descriptive case study (Yin): 6 semi-structured interviews with supervising professors and an open-ended student questionnaire in two rounds (32 responses); thematic analysis (Braun & Clarke), inductive coding by researcher pairs, themes then compared with the SPACE dimensions

context.claude: Academic; two-semester SE capstone program (SEN) with real external clients in a Brazilian undergraduate SE course; 6 professors, 32 students
context.nlm: Academic; SEN capstone program with real external clients at UFMS, Brazil; 6 professors, 32 students
context.value: academic; two-semester software engineering capstone program (SEN) with real clients in a Brazilian undergraduate SE course (authors at UFMS); 6 supervising professors interviewed, 32 student questionnaire responses (of 46 invited per round)

space_applied.note: Both call SPACE 'APPLIED', but Claude describes it as a lens against which inductive themes were compared, NotebookLM as the baseline to categorize perceptions. Paper: themes derived first, then 'compared our results to SPACE'; professors' theme map is labelled with SPACE dimension names.

ai_discussed.note: AI only as transcription tools (Riverside, TurboScribe) and one related-work mention of Copilot studies.

remote_covid.note: On-site work (attendance tracked on in-person days).

data_window.note: Claude: questionnaire rounds after the 2024.2 and 2025.1 semesters; NotebookLM gives only two rounds/semesters without dates.

cat_productivity.note: Perceived signs, not measured: artifact/task deliveries, cards, story points delivered (both extractors label these Activity).

cat_quality.note: Deliverable quality and bugs/fixes discussed as a Performance sign, 'hard to measure'.

cat_collaboration.note: Communication & collaboration signs: team dynamics, peer feedback, engagement with the client.

cat_satisfaction.note: Satisfaction & well-being signs (team tension, student frustration) in professors' map; work-life balance as contextual factor.

cat_activity.note: Volume and distribution of commits checked occasionally by professors; work hours and attendance.

cat_delivery.note: Claude labels deliveries/delays 'Delivery' and self-reported task start-to-finish time 'lead time', but these are task-level (productivity/planning), not delivery-pipeline metrics.

cat_agile.note: Estimate accuracy and delays within sprints observed in Scrum ceremonies (dailies, sprint reviews).

cat_survey.note: Interviews and questionnaire on perceptions of productivity; self-perceived productivity item.

evidence.quote: To answer them, we conducted a descriptive case study [37] in SEN.
We conducted six semi-structured interviews with professors and administered a questionnaire to students. We used thematic analysis to understand their perspectives.
After deriving the subthemes and themes, we compared our results to SPACE [9], to consider to which extent professors and students matched the framework dimensions.
Finalyear students enroll in SEN for two semesters to participate in capstone projects with real clients.
We also sent the questionnaire to a total of 46 students, and got 26 responses. Altogether, we obtained 32 responses.
Productivity was measured by the number of cards, resolutions, bugs, and story points delivered.
that can include metrics like the number of commits, basically what they're submitting.
One of its subtheme states that quality is important to software delivery, while another acknowledges that quality is related to productivity, but hard to measure
Both professors and students report signs on performance, activity, communication and collaboration (the PAC of SPACE).

For supervisors, some satisfaction and well-being signs are key to understanding students' productivity. Two relevant subthemes regarding this are the existence of team tension and of student frustration
Finally, professors also consider delays as a pattern of underdelivery, leading students to deliver less in the available time. It has implications for their estimates.
This can be noticed when they fail to complete their task within the estimated time.
